scope: Finite18-row gap table from same authorized read-only reviewer; current documented mandatory core, not allSDKs. No app runtime prerequisite.
patch_findings: 07–09 and four inherited mirrors independently accepted; no remaining P0–P3 in reviewed corrections. Whole-core breadth has separate finite gaps.

items.gap: Map nine quality gates to existing specialist chains

resolution.semantic_support: Nine gates bind respectively architecture; language/concurrency; UI/accessibility/localization; persistence/media; networking/sync; identity/security/platform; build/supply-chain; testing/performance/operations; release/StoreKit. Specialist rows below provide theory/depth/route/aid/evidence. Verification exclusions override execution plans, not design requirements.

Generic parameters preserve caller-selected type relationships; opaque results hide one producer-chosen concrete type; boxed existential permits runtime heterogeneity with lost static relationships. Owner example chooses the boundary rather than blanket any/some replacement.

Checked continuations require exactly one resume; omitted resume leaks suspended resources. AsyncStream default buffer is unbounded; producer termination/cancellation and bounded overflow policy need explicit ownership. Cancellation is cooperative, not an automatic callback undo.

Container parent/child lifecycle and appearance ownership differ from SwiftUI representable lifecycle. SwiftUI owns represented root layout; coordinator bridges callbacks. Scene/window state and adaptive layout remain owned at their actual scope.

CoreAI artifact/runtime specialization and load/inference costs are explicit boundaries. Typed generated tool arguments are not authorization; concurrent tool invocations require independent side-effect policy. Required tool loops need an exit; local evaluation thresholds are operating policy, not Apple API guarantees.

Target defines module/import/access and resource boundary; products export usable targets. Bundle.module is generated for actual SwiftPM resources, not an app-wide lookup rule or permission to migrate integration.

Content worlds isolate JavaScript variables, not the shared DOM. Navigation changes execution context; message handler reply/lifetime and origin/frame/operation validation belong to the app bridge. Association or received script message alone is not authorization.

Server challenge/public credential binding and relying-party identity govern passkeys. SIWA stable user identifier and current credential state govern account access; revoked/not-found returns to authentication. Email availability is not inferred from an abstract-only source.

items.gap: Cryptography key/nonce lifecycle, failure and alternative

resolution.semantic_support: AES-GCM authenticates ciphertext/AAD; reuse of nonce under one key violates the primitive. Authentication failure must not expose plaintext. Key rotation/version ownership and Keychain alternative are in the failure example; ThisDeviceOnly restricts cross-device migration, not every backup.

Server/client/ancestor conflict merge must preserve server change tag. Change tokens are scoped incremental cursors, not object versions. Persist engine serialized state across launches; account changes clear engine pending changes and require explicit reconciliation of app-owned work without cross-account replay.

items.gap: MatchingUUID/dSYM crash identity and competing hang hypotheses

resolution.semantic_support: dSYM must match binary UUID; symbol names without build identity do not establish root cause. Crash and hang analysis compare plausible thread/actor/work hypotheses; sampled main-thread work and waiting are distinct. Hang source tail was not read; only inspected sections support this claim.

Build scripts declare inputs/outputs and failure status so graph ordering is real. Source membership and generated/resource consumers need one producer. Package resolution pins source state; binary manifest checksum validates artifact bytes separately.

Domain association requires matching website file and entitlement but does not authorize an entity operation. App Groups grant a shared container/IPC boundary; target capabilities and older-consumer schema compatibility remain separate responsibilities.

items.gap: PhotoKit limited/changing permission and provider/cloud asset lifetime

resolution.semantic_support: Limited library access is selected-subset and can change; picker grant differs from broad PhotoKit permission. Cloud asset access needs network policy/progress and stale-result rejection. Provider scope must survive copying; source availability is not durable app ownership.

Metric reports/diagnostics have delivery and identity scope, not immediate per-action proof. Dynamic string/object log privacy differs from numeric defaults; explicit redaction remains necessary. Existing rollout/kill-switch and recovery contracts bind observation to release identity; conceptual scenarios are not incident execution.

App and each SDK declare applicable required-reason usage in their own privacy manifests; SDK cannot rely on app manifest. Listed SDK binary distribution signature requirements are conditional, not a blanket all-SDK rule. Review/privacy/distribution facts require current release-specific checking.

Grace permits continued access; billing-retry label alone does not prove entitlement. Verified transaction/current entitlement, expiration/revocation and family context govern access. Recovery example preserves another still-valid entitlement and finishes only after delivery.

items.gap: Locale/Calendar/TimeZone display-vs-wire and package/target bundle lookup

resolution.semantic_support: Localized display uses user locale/calendar/timezone as appropriate; fixed wire format uses explicit stable serialization rules. Catalog plural/format semantics and target/package bundle lookup are separate; SwiftPM resource lookup applies only to adopted package targets.
